Entry: only JSR mark_to_draw (render.6502:473), right after classify; the labels are local, and width_of_type_A has no caller (its name only appears in a comment), so deleting it is safe. classify_xh holds LO(rec_xh)|boff (&80 or &C0), with HI fixed at &B5, and boff does not change between classify and the call. So c3_rec's rec_xh+boff,X reads the same byte as the old TXA/ADC boff/TAY/LDA rec_xh,Y. C is clear there and the ASSERT keeps it in the page, so there is no wrap difference (X < MOVER_SLOTS). Coming into mark_to_draw, need is only 0 or &80 (classify STZ, then &80), and each slot's work reads only that slot's need plus the mover tables, so walking the list in reverse gives the same need bytes. Y bookkeeping: each path back to .each has Y = index (BNE/BMI each directly, or next's LDY ren_k(=index-1)/INY). With act_n = 0, DEY gives &FF and BMI done is taken; act_n < 64, so BMI is safe. The callee (game.6502:2259) clobbers A and Y, uses X as the type, and reads &C5 and mover_x_low. It does not touch ren_i, ren_k or the stack, and it returns with C as its result. PHX/PLX are balanced, PLX keeps C, and X = slot for the need |= &40 tail, the same as the old LDX ren_i. The old code also wrote ren_i, which the new code leaves stale. Nothing reads it before close_over_overlaps' gather writes it, and that read only happens when act_n > 0. Old and new also differ in A, X, Y and the flags at RTS (old Y=act_n, Z=C=1; new Y=&FF, N=1). Neither is live: the next instruction is JSR close_over_overlaps, which starts STZ list_n / LDY #0. Interrupts: the IRQ does not use ren_k/ren_i/&C5/act/need. The extra stack byte under the JSR is harmless, and the self-modified operand is in bank 4 code that the IRQ leaves paged back. Bytes: the old &9790-&97CA is 59 bytes and the new is 52, so 7 bytes are freed. Cycles: the staying-slot path drops from 42 to 23 cycles, a candidate slot saves about 5, and the setup costs +9 (exit 1 cycle cheaper). That fits the measured -19.4 a pass.
